correctness.rationale: Reconstructed for n>=3 and R>0: normalization R=1, squared distance on every edge strictly convex, angular test bounds strict distance peaks by two even or three odd. The opposite even side yields two crossings plus two on complement for all nonvertex centers; vertex chains are monotone. For odd n, an interior projection supplies at least four crossings; both opposite-edge projections have interior feet when t<tau_n. The weak-peak/strong-valley squared gap factors as c²(t-t_-)(t-t_+), where t_-=(2s/c)(1-cos(alpha/2))² and t_+>s. It is positive exactly |t|<t_-; at equality two doubled crossings degenerate into one tangent/vertex each, so the maximum is four. The normalized perimeter ratio equals tau_n/s and its Taylor leading term is pi^4/(32n^4). Independent exact symbolic difference factorization passed, and fresh radius-chamber enumeration checked 80 representative centers across n=3..101, including both sides of the threshold. Finite tests supplement, not replace, the all-n geometric proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2013 primary journal article and corresponding thesis chapter introduce the best-center invariant N(K), the sets J(K,m), general existence/finite bounds and a special 15-gon, but neither establishes the all-center spectrum of regular polygons nor the exact J(P_n,6) arcs or n^-4 density. The closest published polygon-complexity result concerns min_p H_K(p), and a related farthest-distance profile retains only max_q ||p-q||, insufficient to reconstruct how many level-set intersections occur at intermediate radii. Targeted published-record searches did not locate a dominating equivalent theorem; this is a best-of-knowledge conclusion subject to residual historical risk.
residual_risks: An older unindexed geometric note may have computed the same exact regular-polygon six-center window; searches do not establish absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The primary 2013 problem explicitly asks for sets J(K,m) and their relative boundary measures. The result supplies a complete natural-family classification of H_n(p) and J(P_n,6), including the strict algebraic edge-midpoint window and exact n^-4 rarity. This quantifies variation over centers that cannot be recovered from the established best-center N(K), so the precise invariant and asymptotic are independently useful.
